SAF-DRV-RASH.desc: Rash or dangerous driving. Ref: Motor Vehicles Act 1988 s.184 (verify).

SAF-DRV-DISTRACT.desc: Distracted driving, including phone or screen use. Ref: MV Act s.184, handheld-device clause (verify).

SAF-OTHER.desc: Any other risk of physical harm to riders or the public, such as a vehicle defect, an unsafe stop or an assault.

PAY-NO-PASS.desc: Rider paid, or tried to pay, but the pass or booking is not active.

PAY-DOUBLE-CHARGE.desc: Rider was charged more than once for the same thing.

PAY-REFUND.desc: Refund owed to the rider and not received.

OPS-AC.desc: AC broken, off, or set to the wrong temperature.

OPS-ROUTE-CHANGE.desc: Stop or route changed without telling riders.

OPS-COMFORT.desc: Crowding, cleanliness, wifi or other onboard comfort.

APP-BUG.desc: App crash, logout, or a broken or confusing screen.

REQ-FEATURE.desc: Request for something new, or a how-to question.

SENT-PRICE.desc: Complaint about price or value with no specific incident.

OTHER.desc: A real issue that fits no other code.

NONE.desc: No issue: praise or a neutral note.

safety.title: Driver safety
safety.fix: Today, for each incident: confirm the bus and driver from the trip record, then take a confirmed driver off duty pending review, and reply to the rider. FB-005's route code is a Hyderabad route but it names Powai in Mumbai, so confirm the bus first.
safety.cost: Not deferred. Every safety incident gets same-day verify-then-act.
safety.risk: A crash that injures riders or the public, possibly children at a school crossing. Legal liability, regulatory action against our permits, and the kind of public incident that can end a commute business.
asks: Telematics on every bus, so harsh driving is caught without waiting for a rider
A dedicated driver phone with no distracting apps
Random, unannounced safety inspectors on buses

money.title: Money taken, nothing delivered
money.fix: Today: check each rider against the payment provider's records. Riders with no active pass and a debit, a pending payment or at least one attempt keep riding until we verify; anyone let through without a confirmed debit is flagged for review. Verified paid: activate the pass. Not paid: ask them to pay, or stop the free rides. Return the double charge. Trace the stuck refund before it passes the refund window. Reply to every affected rider. Engineering on-call investigates why successful payments are not activating passes.
money.cost: No rider pays twice to get to work. Riders owed money wait one more day for it. Cityflo pays the rest: free rides for riders not yet verified, and a support queue that grows as every new renewal hits the same fault.
money.risk: Every renewal can hit the same fault: mass cancellations, payment disputes, a growing refund liability, and public reviews about being charged for nothing. Pass renewals are core recurring revenue.
money.owner: Payments engineering, with support for replies

late.title: Late buses
late.fix: Analyse on-time data and re-optimise schedules. Fix the worse direction first (this batch points to the morning commute), and re-optimise for the days each route runs late. On the Hyderabad route, schedule pressure may be behind the rash driving.
late.cost: Riders on these routes are likely late to work again tomorrow and some miss connections. Riders pay in time; Cityflo pays in repeat tickets and trust.
late.risk: Riders who need to reach work on time switch to cabs, and the premium promise stops meaning anything. Schedule pressure keeps feeding rash driving.

ac.title: AC problems
ac.fix: Maintenance check on buses where AC is not cooling. Keep the cabin at a comfortable temperature relative to outside: cooler when it's hot, warmer when it's cold.
ac.cost: Another hot ride tomorrow on the affected buses. Riders pay in comfort; Cityflo pays in trust and repeat tickets.
ac.risk: AC is part of what riders pay a premium for. Left broken through hot months, riders stop seeing the value.

route.title: Route and stop changes
route.fix: Every stop or route change notifies affected riders before it happens. A stranded rider is an operational gap. An unannounced route change on a safety route goes to the safety review.
route.cost: If another stop moves without notice, more riders are stranded and may pay for another way to work.
route.risk: Riders stop trusting stops and the map. Unannounced route changes can hide unsafe or unauthorised detours.
route.owner: Route operations, with product for notifications

comfort.title: Onboard comfort
comfort.fix: Check occupancy on crowded routes for another bus. Dirty seats are not acceptable: clean now and put a better cleaning schedule in place. Wifi is cut until more riders report it.
comfort.cost: Crowding continues until occupancy is checked; riders pay in comfort.
comfort.risk: Chronic crowding pushes riders away. Dirty buses erode the premium promise.

app.title: Booking app bugs
app.fix: Fix the booking flow first: crashes and mid-booking logouts. Then simplify or remove confusing screens. Fewer features that work beat more that don't. Check whether a crash mid-booking can leave a payment with no pass.
app.cost: Some riders fail to book or have to start over. Riders pay in time; Cityflo pays in lost bookings.
app.risk: Riders who can't book stop trying, and store ratings drop. If linked to payments, each failed booking can add a paid-but-no-pass case.

tracking.title: Live tracking lag
tracking.fix: No fleet-wide fix on one report. Check tracking accuracy on the routes with safety incidents first. If lag clusters at night or on risky stretches, it becomes a safety issue.
tracking.cost: Low. Tracking may lag a few minutes for another day.
tracking.risk: If the lag is real on safety routes, telematics would detect harsh driving late exactly where it matters.

requests.title: Feature requests
requests.fix: Log, don't build, until existing features work. Every direct question gets a reply. Extra stops only if they bring riders for a small time cost, after route analysis.
requests.risk: Low. A rider who can't pause a pass may cancel instead.

sentiment.title: Price and value complaints
sentiment.fix: Check whether the price is fair against occupancy data and per-ride unit economics. No action on a single review.
sentiment.cost: One rider's frustration; possibly one lost renewal.
sentiment.risk: If it reflects a wider view, price-sensitive riders cancel at renewal.

other.title: Needs a human look
other.fix: Fits no code. Read it and label it by hand.

unlabelled.title: Not labelled
unlabelled.fix: No label for these messages (mock mode only has labels for the 30-message batch). Run with --live, or label them by hand below.
unlabelled.risk: Unknown. A safety message could be sitting here.
